notes_endorse: Editorial endorses Eisenhower for 'clean, honest leadership.' Paper notes 'we ARE NOT JOINING THE REPUBLICAN RANKS, but we are joining in with the South Carolinians for Eisenhower, because we believe that to vote independent is more favorable to the South which we love'

Editorial 'Voters Face Important Decisions Tuesday' (Nov 1, 1974) — 'Jo Ann Price is by far the better qualified of the two candidates in every respect. Has served the past two years in this post and has steadfastly demonstrated that she is conscientious, hard-working.'

Editorial 'Voters Face Important Decisions Tuesday' (Nov 1, 1974) — 'personable and alert, and his record demonstrates ambition and a willingness to serve... His youth and energy, plus a sound feel for this area should bring a plus factor to the commission.' Recommended over incumbent Edwin B. Farmer.
Editorial 'Voters Face Important Decisions Tuesday' (Nov 1, 1974) — 'we recommend a vote for L. J. (Larry) Murphy, the incumbent. Mr. Murphy is easily the best qualified person for this seat.'

Editorial 'Voters Face Important Decisions Tuesday' (Nov 1, 1974) — 'Carrol H. Warner prefers return to office from Area No. 4. He has demonstrated a level-headed, calm and straightforward attitude in his service for two years in this capacity.' Incumbent.

Editorial 'Voters Face Important Decisions Tuesday' (Nov 1, 1974) — 'Marshall Cain is the person who will best represent the people of this area. Mr. Cain has a statewide reputation as an honest, hard-working public servant who puts the welfare of his state ahead of politics and petty demagoguery.' Recommended over Mrs. Irene K. Rudnick.

Editorial 'Voters Face Important Decisions Tuesday' (Nov 1, 1974) — 'Cecil L. Collins merits return to office. He is well qualified and has served in the State House of Representatives with distinction.' Incumbent.

Editorial 'Voters Face Important Decisions Tuesday' (Nov 1, 1974) — 'In the District 64 race, M. Judson Barber, 27, has all the makings of an outstanding public servant for this area.' (NOTE: original 2026-04 extraction incorrectly recorded this as 'BRANDY' with notes from a different race; corrected in re-QA 2026-05-26.)
Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — recommended for County Council Chairman. Clearly the best choice over incumbent vice chairman Charles W. Prosser.

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — incumbent in District 7. 'Cullinan for two years has been a voice of reason in the storm-tossed Council. He is faithful to his responsibilities; he is conscientious; he is knowledgeable.' OCR variation: name appears as both CULLINS and CULLINAN.
Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'District 1 we believe will return Lucas Ray to office. Mr. Ray has clearly demonstrated his fitness.' Incumbent.

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'District 2 offers a pair of relatively new faces. Both candidates have impressive accomplishments in their respective fields. We believe James F. Pettigrew is best qualified.'

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'District 3 likely will have no trouble deciding to elect Marvin E. Dunbar. He is one of the bright hopes for a new and effective Council.' (NOTE: original extraction had 'MELVIN'; corrected to MARVIN in re-QA 2026-05-26.)

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'District 4 will have a choice of a political newcomer, Miss Woodring, and a controversial incumbent, Cleve Edmonds. Mrs. Woodring has much to recommend her election. She is intelligent.' First name not visible in scan.
Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — recommended for District 5 over Laurie Livingston. First name not legible in scan.

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'District 6 offers a new personality in politics. He is Walter F. Gee, Jr., a school teacher. While he is reserved, he chooses his words well. He says what he means and means what he says. His election would be an appreciable asset to the council direction.' (NOTE: original extraction split this single endorsement into two erroneous records, MCGEE/HOMER at Dist 6 and GUY/WALTER at Dist 8; consolidated and corrected in re-QA 2026-05-26.)

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'The Aiken Standard recommends re-election of Sheriff Paul D. Grant.' Incumbent. (NOTE: original extraction had 'PARK' due to OCR error; corrected to PAUL in re-QA 2026-05-26.)

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'Shirley Langston can be relied upon to serve faithfully, honestly and impartially as auditor.' (NOTE: original extraction incorrectly placed Langston in SOLICITOR office; corrected to AUDITOR in re-QA 2026-05-26.)

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'For treasurer we commend Marjia B. Pinckard.' Name uncertain due to scan quality. (NOTE: original extraction had 'BENNETT, MURIEL' which does not match the clipping; corrected in re-QA 2026-05-26 with best-guess name.)

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'For register of mesne conveyances our wholehearted recommendation is for the election of Virginia B. Brennan.' Last name uncertain due to scan quality.

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — incumbent. 'Gilbert E. McMillan, Michael L. Laughlin, and A. J. Dooley are the incumbents, and they have demonstrated their effectiveness in working with the Aiken County General Assembly for the benefit of Aiken County. They have established seniority. No reason not to return them with enthusiasm.'

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — incumbent. Endorsed jointly with McMillan and Dooley. (NOTE: original extraction had 'LAXGO' due to OCR error; corrected to LAUGHLIN in re-QA 2026-05-26.)
Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — incumbent. Endorsed jointly with McMillan and Laughlin.

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'Newcomers vie for Seat 4. They are Addison G. (Joe) Wilson and Nick G. Setzler. Mr. Wilson offers one of the brightest and most dedicated young minds to come upon the scene in many years. His accomplishments in the public service arena during his relatively few years are most impressive. He is personable, honest, industrious.' Setzler is named but only Wilson endorsed.

Editorial 'Appraising The Candidates' (Oct 29, 1976) — 'STATE HOUSE / District 65 — [first name unclear] W. Dunkin, an accountant, against the entrenched Rep. Irene K. Rudnick. We believe Aiken County's best interests would be served by Mr. Dunkin.' First name partially obscured in scan.
